subject: Procurement readiness & commercial path — Redwood Inference
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood follow-up: procurement readiness & next steps

Hi Samira — thanks for a productive discovery earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has what they need to move forward:

Key takeaways from call:
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant for care coordinators (low-latency text gen, PII-handling)
- Target go-live: Q4 2026 (pilot in Sep)
- Security bar: SOC 2, VPC/private deployment for PHI, customer KMS for private option
- Buying constraints: prefer PO/NET30 via centralized procurement; also evaluate marketplace option (AWS Marketplace) if it speeds procurement

Commercial options to consider (we'll align with procurement):
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest time-to-value, pay-as-you-go, per-token pricing, ideal for pilot/proof-of-value.
2) Dedicated — reserved GPU pool, committed throughput, better unit economics (commits).
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — for PHI workloads; platform fee + infra costs; longer procurement & onboarding cadence.

Requested items I can share right now:
- SOW draft and pricing grid (attached).
- Short T&C summary + sample MSA (I can send via DocuSign when you're ready).

Next steps:
1) Can procurement confirm whether PO/NET30 is required or if card is acceptable for pilot?
2) Are you able to evaluate AWS Marketplace procurement (this can shorten approvals)?
3) I'll loop in Aditya (SE) for a short technical sizing recommendation (hosted vs dedicated sizing).

If this matches your notes, I propose a 30-min procurement handoff next week to align the billing path and timing.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf; Redwood_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up: procurement readiness & next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. Procurement here — a few clarifying Qs so we can route internally:

1) Billing method: Our standard is PO with NET30 for anything above $10k/month. For pilots under that threshold we can sometimes use a corporate card but need approval.
2) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred by our procurement team because it integrates with our SAP/Procurement tooling — do you have a listing?
3) Contracts: we need a standard MSA/ordering schedule we can attach to the PO. Are your standard MSA terms compatible with a PO/NET30 workflow?
4) Pricing asks: can you provide a 3-node dedicated committed (12-month) unit price, and an on-demand hosted price estimate for pilot usage (approx. 1M tokens/month)?

Please send SOW + pricing grid and a pointer to any marketplace listing. Procurement will review and get back with a routing timeline (should be 2-3 weeks once we have MSA + pricing).

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Sr. Director, Digital Transformation
Acme Health
samira.khan@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up: procurement readiness & next steps

Samira — looping in Aditya (SE) and Dev (Commercial/Legal) to help answer the procurement questions below and to propose concrete pricing paths. Attaching the SOW + updated pricing grid.

Short answers up front:
- PO/NET30: we accept PO/NET30 for enterprise customers. We'll attach our MSA and an ordering schedule that procurement can use with the PO.
- Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace (private listing available); if you prefer, we can transact there and it will show as an offer in your Marketplace console — this often speeds procurement integration.

Commercial paths for your procurement team to consider (high level):
A) Pilot — Hosted (Redwood API) on on-demand billing. Pros: fastest start, low up-front. Cons: higher unit cost versus commit.
B) Pilot -> Production — transition to Dedicated reserved pool with a commit (e.g., 3-node equivalent) for predictable unit economics. Commit term examples: 12 or 24 months with stepped pricing.
C) Regulated/PHI — Private (VPC) deployment. Typically longer lead time; we include platform license + customer infra. Procurement will likely want a separate charging path (platform fee on invoice + infra pass-through).

Ask from SE: Aditya, can you confirm the sizing assumption for a 3-node dedicated pool vs hosted performance (latency and throughput) for 1M tokens/month so we can present numbers to Samira?

Commercial ask: Dev, can you attach the MSA or indicate typical lead time for contract review / redlines? Procurement wants to know if we can be within a 2-3 week review window.

I'll schedule a 30-min call next Tue (7/13) to review commercial options and pricing scenarios unless you prefer a different time.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf; Redwood_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up: procurement readiness & next steps

Hi all — quick notes from commercial/legal to make procurement routing easier:

1) MSA & ordering schedule: I have the current MSA ready to share (standard Redwood MSA, includes PO/NET30 acceptance language). I can send a redline-first pass within 3 business days; turnaround on customer redlines is typically 2-3 business days after we receive theirs.
2) PO/NET30: we can accept PO/NET30. For on-demand pilot (under $10k) card is fine; for committed deals we require a signed ordering schedule and either PO or wire payment per schedule.
3) Marketplace: we are live on AWS Marketplace (Redwood Inference LLC). If Acme would like to purchase via Marketplace, we can provide a private listing link and procurement can complete purchase through the Marketplace console — note the Marketplace adds a fee and may change invoice handling, but it often shortens procurement approvals.
4) Pricing framing: Attachments contain two bands — hosted on-demand rate card and committed dedicated pricing tiers. For the committed example Samira asked about, see row: "3-node equivalent (12-month) — $X/month (billable via invoice/PO)".

If procurement needs any specific billing language for your SAP system (PO fields, remit-to, tax ids), send sample PO template and I can map fields.

I will upload the MSA and ordering schedule to the DocuSign link once Marissa gives the green light.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa/Dev — this is helpful. Procurement confirmed:
- Preferred path: Marketplace if pricing delta is acceptable (please call out any Marketplace fees). Otherwise standard MSA + PO/NET30 is acceptable.
- We will need the final SOW + ordering schedule to attach to the PO. Please provide the MSA and a clean ordering schedule (PDF) we can present.
- Pricing request: please provide a firm quote for the 3-node committed (12-month) scenario and a hosted on-demand estimate for 1M tokens/month (with expected token price). Also call out any minimum invoice amounts and billing cadence.

Can we lock a 30-min call on Thu 7/15 10:00 AM PT to finalize the procurement path? If so, please send a calendar invite.

Samira
